states: Production vite builds of the tree before and after this change, each on origin/main with the page-owned-state change in place, served by vite preview and proxied to one shared private mock-estate Pulse backend on pulse-dev (50 Proxmox nodes with 929 guests, 7 vSphere hosts with 18 VMs). Real useWorkloadsState, WorkloadsFilter, WorkloadsSurface, GuestRow and production CSS; mock data, not a live estate or authenticated production acceptance.

Three rounds per build and viewport, four before and three after for Proxmox desktop, all on the same backend: WebSocket connected with frames, no console errors, and the same guest rows, columns, table headers, filter-bar controls, node buttons, group counts and API request sets on both builds. Two Proxmox desktop rounds hit Playwright 30 s action timeouts under host load and one round's login returned a backend 500; those three are excluded.
Eight before and after screenshots (Proxmox and vSphere at both widths) inspected side by side: identical layout apart from the mock's live values.
Unminified production builds of both trees differ in exactly 3 of 189 files (Proxmox, Vmware, useWorkloadsState chunks) and the diff is only the removed options and the collapsed enabled branches.
interactions: search with no match then cleared: filtered-empty state and restored rows match on both builds
Proxmox: Show guests on a node scopes the table to that node and Show all nodes clears it; matches on both builds
first guest row click opens its inline detail row on both builds
load and steady-state API requests (union per round) are the same set on both builds
not exercised in a browser: two nodes whose instance and node names join to one string; that attribution is pinned by WorkloadsSurface.performance.contract.test.tsx and its negative control
